rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in ‘they discarded it’ marks haste: later Jewish scholars hurried to discard the covenant when each became capable of interpreting and declaring scripture, using that ability for distortion and concealment.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { فنبذوه } عطف بالفاء الدالة على التعقيب للإشارة إلى مسارعتهم إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fa conveys necessary concomitance: they hastened intensely when circumstances called for it and devoted their attention to doing so.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء مستعملة في لازم التعقيب ، وهو شدة المسارعة لذلك عند اقتضاء الحال إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sequence is assessed separately for each act of distortion and profit: the general covenant covered every case, and each breach followed the covenant applicable to that case.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التعقيب بحسب الحوادث التي أساؤوا فيها التأويل واشتروا بها الثمن القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means throwing or casting; here it metaphorically describes failing to honor a covenant, as if the covenant were an object left unused.
rows.anchor: والنبذ : الطرح والإلقاء ، وهو هنا مستعار لعدم العمل بالعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Behind their backs’ depicts waste and neglect: prized things are kept before the eyes, protected and watched, as in God’s assurance that the Prophet is under His eyes.
rows.anchor: ووراء الظهور هنا تمثيل للإضاعة والإهمال ، لأن شأن الشيء المهتم به المتنافس فيه أن يجعل نصب العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of putting something behind one’s back further develops the metaphor of casting away as breaking the covenant.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التمثيل ترشيح لاستعارة النبذ لإخلاف العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both pronouns refer to the covenant, they treated God’s pledge lightly and exchanged it for little gain, neglecting their pledge to explain scripture and not conceal it.
rows.anchor: يجوز عودهما إلى الميثاق أي استخفوا بعهد الله وعوضوه بثمن قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both pronouns refer to scripture, they neglected the text and its rulings, replacing their implementation for small gain; this entails neglecting both its verses and their meanings.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عودهما إلى الكتاب أي أهملوا الكتاب ولم يعتنوا به ، والمراد إهمال أحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This continues the account of the People of the Book after their betrayal in transmitting religion, portraying another group that commits disgraceful acts and then seeks praise instead of remorse or concealment.
rows.anchor: تكملة لأحوال أهل الكتاب المتحدث عنهم ببيان حالة خلقهم بعد أن بين اختلال أمانتهم في تبليغ الدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed reported view says the verse was revealed about hypocrites; the address can apply to anyone fit to receive it, while the relative clause identifies a particular Jewish or hypocritical group.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في المنافقين ، والخطاب لكل من يصلح له الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the apparent reading, they rejoice in the earlier abandonment of scripture and its sale for little gain, specifically in the worldly benefit they obtained.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { يفرحون بما أتوا } أنهم يفرحون بما فعلوا مما تقدم ذكره ، وهو نبذ الكتاب والاشتراء به ثمنا قليلا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they want praise as guardians of the law and its learned interpreters, although that description is false.
rows.anchor: هذا ظاهر معنى الآية . وهو قول مجاهد . وعن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they misled their followers away from belief in Muhammad and wanted praise for being learned in religious books.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنهم أتوا إضلال أتباعهم عن الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari says the verse concerns hypocrites who stayed behind from an expedition, offered excuses accepted by the Prophet, and wanted praise as would-be fighters; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري : أنها نزلت في المنافقين

rows.speaker: مروان بن الحكم
rows.claim: In al-Bukhari, Marwan asks Ibn Abbas whether everyone who rejoices in a deed and seeks undeserved praise would be punished, since that would condemn them all.
rows.anchor: وفي ( البخاري ) : أن مروان بن الحكم قال لبوابه : ( اذهب يا رافع إلى ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas answers that the passage concerns Jews who misreported the Prophet’s inquiry to win his approval and rejoiced in concealing the truth, then recites 3:187–188.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ( وما لكم ولهذه إنما دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يهود ، فسألهم عن شيء فأخبروه بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s explanation the relative expression identifies a particular group, not everyone comprehensively.
rows.anchor: وليس الموصول بمعنى لام الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mafāza means a place of safety and success against an enemy; the broad desert is called this because a stranded person can escape enemies and avengers there, and people sought refuge in it.
rows.anchor: والمفازة : مكان الفوز . وهو المكان الذي من يحله يفوز بالسلامة من العدو

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha’s cited lines describe the forbidding desert where caravans are held up and people fend off pursuers, illustrating the refuge sense associated with mafāza.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة : أو أضع البيت في صماء مظلمة تقيد العير لا يسري بها الساري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ‘place of success’ is general, the verse specifies that the success sought is safety from punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت المفازة مجملة بالنسبة للفوز الحاصل فيها بين ذلك بقوله : { من العذاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min can mean exchange, as in 88:7, or ‘away from’ through construing mafāza as deliverance; both explain escape from punishment.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( من ) معناه البدلية ، مثل قوله تعالى : { لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Abu Jafar read the first ‘yaḥsabanna’ with ya for third-person report; the other readers use the second-person ta.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن كثير ، وابن عامر ، وأبو عمور ، وأبو جعفر : لا يحسبن الذين يفرحون بالياء التحتية على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisai, Abu Jafar, and Yaqub read the sīn in taḥsabanna with kasra; the remaining readers use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وأما سين ( تحسبن ) فقرأها بالكسر نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، والكسائي ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verb of thinking omits its second object because the following ‘do not think them…’ supplies it; the omitted object is ‘themselves.’
rows.anchor: إذ حذف المفعول الثاني لفعل الحسبان الأول لدلالة ما يدل عليه وهو مفعول { فلا تحسبنهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated verb is a parenthetical clause introduced by fa, and ‘safe from punishment’ serves as the second object for both verbs; omission first creates anticipation.
rows.anchor: وأعيد فعل الحسبان في قوله : { فلا تحسبنهم } ( آل عمران : 188 ) مسندا إلى المخاطب على طريقة الاعتراض بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority reading with ta, the first address is indefinite so it includes every listener, while the parenthetical second address is to the Prophet; omission of the first object heightens suspense.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة الجمهور : { لا تحسبن الذين يفرحون } ( آل عمران : 188 ) بتاء الخطاب يكون خطابا لغير معين ليعم كل مخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use singular-address fatḥa in the final taḥsabannahum; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub use plural-address ḍamma, and their initial third-person reading makes the people think themselves safe.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فلا تحسبنهم : بفتح الباء الموحدة على أن الفعل لخطاب الواحد ؛ وقرأه ابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، ويعقوب بضم الباء الموحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With third-person ya and plural ḍamma, the thinkers and those thought of are the same; this reflexive use is characteristic of verbs of supposition and only a few others, including wajada, adima, and faqada.
rows.anchor: واتحاد الفاعل والمفعول للفعل الواحد من خصائص أفعال الظن كما هنا وألحقت بها أفعال قليلة ، وهي : ( وجد ) و ( عدم ) و ( فقد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause ‘created you from one soul’ draws attention to wondrous creation and invites reflection; humanity’s common father supports Islam’s universal call, unlike laws restricted to particular peoples.
rows.anchor: ووصل { خلقكم } بصلة { من نفس واحدة } إدماج للتنبيه على عجيب هذا الخلق وحقه بالاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that Muhammad is especially entitled to the polytheists’ allegiance because he is their kinsman.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تعريض للمشركين بأن أولى الناس بأن يتبعوه هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه من ذوي رحمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common origin prepares for the surah’s later rules that depend on descent and kinship.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تمهيد لما سيبين في هذه السورة من الأحكام المرتبة على النسب والقرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single soul is Adam and the spouse is Hawwa; the apparent meaning of ‘from it’ is that Hawwa was brought forth from Adam’s rib.
rows.anchor: والنفس الواحدة : هي آدم . والزوج : حواء ، فإن حواء أخرجت من آدم . من ضلعه ، كما يقتضيه ظاهر قوله : { منها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: Hawwa was created from part of Adam, either from the remnant of his clay or, as the apparent hadith in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections says, from a rib.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) تبعيضية . ومعنى التبعيض أن حواء خلقت من جزء من آدم . قيل : من بقية الطينة التي خلق منها آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that ‘from it’ merely means ‘from its kind’ adds nothing, since the female of every species belongs to that species.
rows.anchor: ومن قال : إن المعنى وخلق زوجها من نوعها لم يأت بطائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses ‘created her spouse’ and ‘spread from them’ are second and third relative qualifications: the wondrous creator merits reverence, and common descent confirms humanity’s connection despite descending through pairs.
rows.anchor: وعطف قوله : { وخلق منها زوجها } على { خلقكم من نفس واحدة } ، فهو صلة ثانية . وقوله : { وبث منهما } صلة ثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three clauses detail how people were created from one soul; the order first states the creation generally, then details its wonder as the context requires.
rows.anchor: وقد حصل من ذكر هذه الصلات تفصيل لكيفية خلق الله الناس من نفس واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith says Hawwa was created from Adam’s rib; on this account min marks the point of origin, meaning her creation was brought forth from his rib.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في الحديث : أن حواء خلقت من ضلع آدم ، فلذلك يكون حرف ( من ) في قوله : { وخلق منها } للابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Spouse’ here is the first woman from whom humanity descended; each partner can conventionally be called zawj, although the word originally names the pair together.
rows.anchor: والزوج هنا أريد به الأنثى الأولى التي تناسل منها البشر ، وهي حواء . وأطلق عليها اسم الزوج لأن الرجل يكون منفردا

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma‘i strongly rejected the feminine form zawja and considered it a language error, although the author explains that customary usage made zawj apply to either sex.
rows.anchor: ولذلك استوى فيه الرجل والمرأة لأنه من الوصف بالجامد ، فلا يقال للمرأة ( زوجة ) ، ولم يسمع في فصيح الكلام ، ولذلك عده بعض أهل اللغة لحنا . وكان الأصمعي ينكره أشد الإنكار

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: When confronted with Dhu al-Rumma’s use of zawja, al-Asma‘i dismissed him as colloquial, saying he had long eaten salted food and greens in grocers’ shops.
rows.anchor: فقال : إن ذا الرمة طالما أكل المالح والبقل في حوانيت البقالين ، يريد أنه مولد

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s cited hemistich uses zawja for ‘wife,’ the example raised against al-Asma‘i’s rejection of that feminine form.
rows.anchor: أذو زوجة بالمصر أم ذو خصومة أراك لها بالبصرة العام ثاويا

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s verse likewise uses zawjati for ‘my wife,’ providing another poetic example of the form.
rows.anchor: وقال الفرزدق : وإن الذي يسعى ليفسد زوجتي كساع إلى أسد الشرى يستبيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form became common among jurists as a useful way to distinguish men and women when discussing legal rules.
rows.anchor: وشاع ذلك في كلام الفقهاء ، قصدوا به التفرقة بين الرجل والمرأة عند ذكر الأحكام ، وهي تفرقة حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usage of spouse recalls the earlier account of Adam and his spouse in the surah of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة في سورة البقرة ( 35 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of a spouse from one origin is wondrous and varies in form and traits; men and women are each beneficiaries of the other’s creation, and the species receives the gift of offspring.
rows.anchor: وقد شمل وخلق منها زوجها } العبرة بهذا الخلق العجيب الذي أصله واحد ، ويخرج هو مختلف الشكل والخصائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bathth means spreading and dispersing many things; the scattered people compared to moths illustrate the word.
rows.anchor: والبث : النشر والتفريق للأشياء الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular adjective kathīr describes the plural rijāl because kathīr has the same form with singular and plural; a parallel is the many devotees with a prophet.
rows.anchor: ووصف الرجال ، وهو جمع ، بكثير ، وهو مفرد ، لأن كثير يستوي فيه المفرد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits ‘many’ after women because the adjective after men and the verb ‘spread’ already indicate that the women are numerous.
rows.anchor: واستغنى عن وصف النساء بكثير لدلالة وصف الرجل به ما يقتضيه فعل البث من الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed command to fear God begins the surah’s legislation, especially for Muslims retaining Jahili habits of neglecting relatives’ and orphans’ rights.
rows.anchor: شروع في التشريع المقصود من السورة ، وأعيد فعل { اتقوا } : لأن هذه التقوى مأمور بها المسلمون خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using God’s proper name after ‘your Lord’ instills awe appropriate to legislation; the earlier address ‘fear your Lord’ served encouragement.
rows.anchor: واستحضر اسم الله العلم هنا دون ضمير يعود إلى ربكم لإدخال الروع في ضمائر السامعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You ask one another by Him’ means invoking God when swearing; such mutual invocation signifies utmost reverence, so people should all the more fear Him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { تساءلون به } يسأل بعضكم بعضا به في القسم فالمسايلة به تؤذن بمنتهى العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce tusāʾalūn with a doubled sīn by assimilating the second tāʾ into sīn because they are close in articulation and share voicelessness; Hamza, Asim, al-Kisai, and Khalaf use a light sīn after dropping tāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تساءلون } بتشديد السين لإدغام التاء الثانية ، وهي تاء التفاعل في السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers put al-arḥām in the accusative, coordinated with God’s name; Hamza reads it in the genitive, coordinated with the attached pronoun.
rows.anchor: { والأرحام } قرأه الجمهور بالنصب عطفا على اسم الله . وقرأه حمزة بالجر عطفا على الضمير المجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority’s accusative reading, kinship is to be revered by observing its rights; the construction elides ‘rights,’ and the verse begins legislation connected to the preceding creation account.
rows.anchor: فعلى قراءة الجمهور يكون الأرحام مأمورا بتقواها على المعنى المصدري أي اتقائها ، وهو على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza’s genitive reading exalts kinship, as in the Arab oath ‘I adjure you by God and kin’; the report says Utba was awed while hearing the Prophet recite 41:13 and invoked both.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة يكون تعظيما لشأن الأرحام أي التي يسأل بعضكم بعضا بها ، وذلك قول العرب : ( ناشدتك الله والرحم )

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad objects to coordinating a noun with an attached genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, saying he would leave prayer if an imam recited it that way.
rows.anchor: حتى قال المبرد : ( لو قرأ الإمام بهاته القراءة لأخذت نعلي وخرجت من الصلاة )

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik rightly permits coordination with a genitive pronoun without repeating its preposition; the author calls al-Mubarrad’s rejection narrow-minded and overconfident.
rows.anchor: ولقد أصاب ابن مالك في تجويزه العطف على المجرور بدون إعادة الجار ، فتكون تعريضا بعوائد الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading criticizes Jahili Arabs who invoked kinship in oaths yet neglected its rights and wronged orphan relatives; they also harmed Muhammad despite his kinship and claim to their care.
rows.anchor: إذ يتساءلون بينهم بالرحم وأواصر القرابة ثم يهملون حقوقها ولا يصلونها ، ويعتدون على الأيتام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Hamza’s reading, the kinship clause continues the preceding verse’s meaning about humanity’s shared creation.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة يكون معنى الآية تتمة لمعنى التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inheritance injunction, fī is figurative containment: the testament is treated as enclosed in the affairs of the children because it is closely connected to them; the omitted complement is ‘the inheritance of your children.’
rows.anchor: و { في } هنا للظرفية المجازية ، جعلت الوصية كأنها مظروفة في شأن الأولاد لشدة تعلقها به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted genitive is required because the children themselves cannot contain a testament; context supplies ‘in the inheritance of your children,’ by the same ellipsis required in ‘your mothers are forbidden.’
rows.anchor: لظهور أن ذوات الأولاد لا تصلح ظرفا للوصية ، فتعين تقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘For the male is the share of two females’ explains the testament clause, since its content is the testament’s meaning; fronting the predicate flags the new right of women, who formerly received no inheritance.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين } بيان لجملة { يوصيكم } لأن مضمونها هو معنى مضمون الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on marrying a father’s former wife connects to the prior ban on inheriting women against their will: a son could claim his deceased father’s wife if she was not his mother; the specific, severe ban leads into the list of forbidden women.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها } ( النساء : 19 ) ، والمناسبة أن من جملة أحوال إرثهم النساء كرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā nakaha means ‘the one whom [a father] married’ generically; mā is lighter than man, while the phrase ‘of women’ clarifies that it is a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: و { ما نكح } بمعنى الذي نكح مراد به الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying ‘what your fathers married’ rather than ‘your fathers’ women’ makes clear that the father’s valid marriage contract alone bars the son, even without consummation.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن أن يقال : لا تنكحوا نساء آبائكم ليدل بلفظ نكح على أن عقد الأب على المرأة كاف في حرمة تزوج ابنه إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibitive present addresses future action and therefore also forbids continuing a marriage with a father’s wife if it began before the prohibition.
rows.anchor: والنهي يتعلق بالمستقبل ، والفعل المضارع مع النهي مدلوله إيجاد الحدث في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In law, nikāḥ means the marriage contract for lawful companionship and enjoyment, not intercourse itself; thus marrying a woman validly contracted by one’s father is forbidden even if he never consummated it.
rows.anchor: والنكاح حقيقة في العقد شرعا بين الرجل والمرأة على المعاشرة والاستمتاع بالمعنى الصحيح شرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars construe nikāḥ in 2:230 as intercourse, arguing that a mere second marriage contract cannot make a thrice-divorced woman lawful again and that no Prophetic explanation is needed; the author says he refuted this in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وأما إطلاق النكاح على الوطء بعقد فقد حمل لفظ النكاح عليه بعض العلماء ، وزعموا أن قوله تعالى : فلا تحل له من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating unlawful sex as a lexical meaning of nikāḥ in Arabic is an untenable claim.
rows.anchor: وأما الوطء الحرام من زنى فكونه من معاني النكاح في لغة العرب دعوى واهية

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ and al-Shafi‘i hold that zina does not create marriage prohibitions between the woman and the fornicator’s son or father; this is also narrated from Ikrima from Ibn Abbas and held by al-Zuhri, Rabi‘a, and al-Layth.
rows.anchor: فالذي ذهب إليه مالك في ( الموطأ ) ، والشافعي : أن الزنى لا ينشر الحرمة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, Ibn al-Majishun, al-Awza‘i, and al-Thawri hold that zina does create such a prohibition; Ibn al-Majishun says Malik died holding this view.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة ، وابن الماجشون من أصحاب مالك : الزنى ينشر الحرمة . قال ابن الماجشون : مات مالك على هذا

rows.speaker: ابن المواز
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mawwaz calls the case disliked; the Mudawwana says ‘he separates from her,’ which most interpret as obligatory, while some interpret it as dislike.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المواز : هو مكروه ، ووقع في المدونة ( يفارقها ) فحمله الأكثر على الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The issue prompted an extended debate between al-Shafi‘i and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, cited by al-Jassas and Fakhr al-Din al-Razi.
rows.anchor: وهذه المسألة جرت فيها مناظرة بين الشافعي ومحمد بن الحسن أشار إليها الجصاص في أحكامه ، والفخر في مفاتيح الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What occurred before’ means before revelation; the exception must be construed as ‘there is no sin for what has passed,’ since completed past acts cannot literally be excepted from a future prohibition.
rows.anchor: و { ما قد سلف } هو ما سبق نزول هذه الآية أي إلا نكاحا قد سلف فتعين أن هذا النكاح صار محرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether pre-Islam marriages were allowed to continue is disputed only by some commentators; the author knows no established case or identified proponent, and suggests people likely separated promptly.
rows.anchor: وهذا لم يقل به إلا بعض المفسرين فيما نقله الفخر ، ولم أقف على أثر يثبت قضية معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites four pre-Islam cases—Umar ibn Umayya, Safwan ibn Umayya, Manzur ibn Rayyan, and Hisn ibn Abi Qays marrying their fathers’ wives—and says none is reported to have converted and remained in such a marriage.
rows.anchor: وقد تزوج قبل الإسلام كثير أزواج آبائهم : منهم عمر بن أمية بن عبد شمس ، خلف على زوج أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators take the exception as the punishment implied by the ban, meaning no punishment applies to past acts; the author says this is obvious and needs no exception because pre-Islam deeds would not be presumed punishable.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون الاستثناء من لازم النهي وهو العقوبة أي لا عقوبة على ما قد سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed reading ironically says ‘marry what your deceased fathers married,’ seeming to license some cases so that the impossible exception strengthens the prohibition; the author finds this device far-fetched in legislation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من تأكيد الشيء بما يشبه ضده : أي إن كنتم فاعلين منه فانكحوا ما قد سلف

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha’s line ‘no fault in them except their swords have nicks’ exemplifies an apparent concession that actually intensifies the point through an impossible exception.
rows.anchor: كقول النابغة : ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that past Jahili marriages are acknowledged as valid historical facts that cannot now be undone because the spouses died; their lineages, dowries, inheritances, and children’s descent are recognized, and Muslims voluntarily stopped the practice.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله : { إلا ما قد سلف } قصد منه بيان صحة ما سلف من ذلك في عهد الجاهلية ، وتعذر تداركه الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators resort to figurative readings of the exception or ‘what was married’ because Islam did not uphold such marriages after revelation: the verse calls them indecent, hateful, and an evil way.
rows.anchor: وقد تأول سائر المفسرين قوله تعالى : { إلا ما قد سلف } بوجوه ترجع إلى التجوز في معنى الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqt means hatred; Arabs named marriage to a father’s wife nikāḥ al-maqt, called its perpetrator al-ḍayzan, and called a son born of it muqīt.
rows.anchor: والمقت اسم سمت به العرب نكاح زوج الأب فقالوا نكاح المقت أي البغض ، وسموا فاعل ذلك الضيزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from banning marriage to a father’s wife into listing prohibited relatives; the change from a future prohibition to ‘has been forbidden’ marks the latter as an established rule.
rows.anchor: تخلص إلى ذكر المحرمات بمناسبة ذكر تحريم نكاح ما نكح الآباء وغير أسلوب النهي فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jahiliyya already forbade the relationships Islam forbids except marrying one’s father’s wife and combining two sisters; this explains the latter prohibition’s present-tense wording.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس : ( كان أهل الجاهلية يحرمون ما يحرم الإسلام إلا امرأة الأب والجمع بين الأختين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When prohibition attaches to the names of persons, it means prohibition of the usual act sought from them: eating carrion, drinking wine, and marrying mothers.
rows.anchor: وتعلق التحريم بأسماء الذوات يحمل على تحريم ما يقصد من تلك الذات غالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ummahāt is retained although Arabic dropped the singular forms amah and amaha; a rare poetic ammah occurs in Ibn Kaysan’s cited line.
rows.anchor: والأمهات جمع أمة أو أمهة ، والعرب أماتوا أمهة وأمه وأبقوا جمعه

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan cites a rare form ummah in a line about a woman’s veil being contested in the markets.
rows.anchor: وورد أمة نادرا في قول شاعر أنشده ابن كيسان : تقبلتها عن أمة لك طالما تنوزع في الأسواق منها خمارها

rows.speaker: قصي بن كلاب
rows.claim: A rare form amaha appears in a verse attributed to Qusay ibn Kilab, naming Kinda and Ilyas as the poet’s mother and father.
rows.anchor: وورد أمهة نادرا في بيت يعزى إلى قصي بن كلاب : عند تناديهم بهالل وهبي أمهتي خندف وإلياس أبي

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir supplies a rare plural amāt in a line describing the mothers of al-Akhtal as disgraceful.
rows.anchor: وجاء أمات قليلا في قول جرير : لقد ولد الأخيطل أم سوء مقلدة من الأمات عارا

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Ra‘i’s line supports the view that amāt is used specifically for non-rational beings; the author says the original singular may have been umm or ummaha, with a deleted form restored in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أمات خاص بما لا يعقل ، قال الراعي : كانت نجائب منذر ومحرق أماتهن وطرقهن فحيلا
